Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + suggested next step

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and one proposed next step so we don’t lose momentum: 

Key points I heard from you:
- Primary need: reduce inference cost for real-time recommendations while keeping 95th-percentile latency under 150ms.
- Volume profile: spiky traffic (peak traffic windows around 11:00–13:00 PDT), average 120k reqs/day.
- Constraints: data residency in US, strict audit requirements, and an internal SRE team who owns deployment.

How Redwood can help (high level):
- Dedicated serving with prefix caching to lower token cost during recurring sequences.
- Quantization profile and kernel selection to hit your latency target on T4-equivalent hardware.
- Private deployment option for isolated audit logs and KMS integration.

Suggested next step: a short scoped pilot (2 weeks) to validate latency and cost on a representative traffic slice. I recommend a 20-minute kickoff to agree on the success metric (e.g., 20% unit cost reduction with equal output quality) and a minimal dataset to run the pilot.

I attached a one-page summary of my notes (discovery-notes.pdf) and a sample agenda for the kickoff. If a pilot doesn’t make sense, a 15-minute call to share rough benchmarking numbers also works.

Open to whatever is easiest for you — are you available next week for a quick sync?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

Ben —

If Alicia hasn’t replied to the first bump, a different framing might help. A couple quick suggestions: 

1) Offer a risk-free short trial: 2 weeks, limited to 1–2 endpoints, with $5k credits and a one-page success checklist (latency + sample-quality proxy).
2) Ask a concrete question up front: "Is cost reduction or latency the higher priority for Q3 planning?" That forces a binary response and helps qualify.
3) If silence persists, try an executive nudge later — short note from an AE manager offering a one-time pilot credit and a named timeline.

I drafted two sentences you can paste into the next email (keeps it tight):

"If helpful, we can run a 2-week, no-cost pilot (up to $5k in credits) focused on 1–2 critical endpoints. Could you confirm whether cost reduction or latency is the priority so we can scope the pilot appropriately?"

If you want, I can be cc'ed on the next message as a gentle escalation.

-Jordan

Following up one last time on this thread. Short and practical option if you’re still evaluating:

- Goal: validate whether we can reduce unit inference cost by ~20% at your 95th-percentile latency target.
- Timeline: kickoff within 3 business days of sign-off; pilot runs ~10 business days; one short wrap call to review metrics.

Could you let me know by end of next week if this is still something you want to explore? If not, a quick note saying "not a priority" will help me close the loop.

If it helps to see a sample pilot scope, I attached the outline (pilot-scope.pdf).
